title: Detection of Trypanosoma cruzi by Indirect Methods: IIF, ELISA, and IHA
author: Claudia Méndez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.62khgcw

steps.title: Perform Indirect Immunofluorescent (IIF) Staining
steps.instruction: Detect T. cruzi antibodies using antigen-impregnated glass slides.

substeps.instruction: Deposit 12 µL of patient and control serum (previously serially diluted in base 2 from 1:8 to 1:256 with buffer) into the antigen wells.
Incubate at 37 °C and wash.
Add anti-human IgG labeled with fluorescein and Evans Blue as a conjugate, incubate, and wash again.
Perform a final washing step and allow to dry at room temperature.
Observe under fluorescence microscopy; samples with fluorescence ≥ 1:32 are considered positive.

steps.title: Perform ELISA for T. cruzi
steps.instruction: Use commercial kits (e.g., ELISA CHAGAS III GRUPOBIOS SA or ELISA CHAGAS T. cruzi Ab DIAPRO) to detect antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Incubate diluted patient serum and corresponding kit controls on antigen-coated plates at 37 °C.
Wash the plates to remove unbound antibodies.
Add 100 µL of conjugate (peroxidase-labeled human anti IgG) and incubate.
Wash the plates.
Add 100 µL of conjugate reacting with peroxidase and incubate at room temperature to reveal color.
Stop the reaction by adding sulfuric acid.
Measure color intensity using a colorimetric ELISA plate reader with a 450 nm filter.

steps.title: Interpret ELISA Results
steps.instruction: Calculate results based on the specific kit used.

substeps.instruction: For ELISA CHAGAS III GRUPOBIOS SA: Calculate cut off as (average of positive controls + average of negative controls) * 0.35. Positive: > cut off + 10%; Negative: < cut off + 10%; Doubtful: cut off +/- 10%.

For ELISA CHAGAS T. cruzi Ab DIAPRO: Calculate cut-off value as average absorbance of negative controls + 0.35. Calculate patient result as (patient sample absorbance / cut-off value). Positive: 1.1; Negative: <0.9; Doubtful: 0.9 - 1.1.

steps.title: Perform Indirect Hemaglutination (IHA) Test
steps.instruction: Use a commercial kit (e.g., Winner) to detect antibodies against T. cruzi.

substeps.instruction: Eliminate heterolipic antibodies by incubating 25 µL of patient and control serum with 25 µL of 2% mercaptoethanol.
Perform serial dilutions on a basis of 1/2 to 1/64 starting from the mercaptoethanol-diluted sample.
Add 25 µL of non-sensitized red blood cells to the 1/2 and 1/4 dilutions as a heterophilia control.
Add 25 µL of IHA antigen (ram red blood cells sensitized with T. cruzi cytoplasmic antigens) to the remaining dilutions.
Wait 90 minutes at room temperature and visualize.
Interpret as positive if a mantle of at least 50% forms on the surface of the well; interpret as negative if there is small agglutination with irregular edges.
